- the next item is the recommendation for second reading (a5-0419/2002) on behalf of the committee on culture, youth, education, the media and sport, on the common position of the council with a view to adopting a european parliament and council decision establishing the european year of education through sport - 2004 [9605/2/2002 - c5-0498/2002 - 2001/0244 (cod)) (rapporteur: mrs pack).
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your reply. we once learned in school that "mens sana in corpore sano" - a healthy mind in a healthy body, and this ancient roman wisdom is familiar to all of us, at least in theory. sport is the most popular leisure activity. one in three europeans is involved in some form of sport, some even into old age. physical activity is good for health, and sports competition also teaches a number of social skills, such as friendship, team spirit, solidarity, performance, assertiveness and, last but not least, fair play. you know, a good athlete is recognized by his victory, a great athlete by his defeat. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. that is why we have been fighting in this parliament for several years to get a legal basis for this in the treaties. i therefore welcome the fact that the commissioner has finally followed the wish expressed in my last report in 1996 and has declared a year of sport. it is not called the year of sport, but for many understandable reasons we call it the year of education through sport 2004. the aim is to highlight the value of extra-curricular education and its educational value in a large number of projects, and to highlight the close partnership between school sports on the one hand and the offer of sports organisations, which are so diverse in europe, on the other. to sum up, the aim and the concern of the 'european year of education through sport 2004' is not to show what people can do in sport - we can see this 365 days a year on dozens of tv channels - but to show what sport can do in human terms and for people. the seven objectives of the theme year are the subject of consensus in this house. the aim is to promote cooperation between educational institutions and sports organisations, social competence through sport, voluntary work, student mobility through international competitions, a balance between mental and physical activity and educational prospects for young professional athletes. the council has confirmed the main points of the report adopted by this house at first reading. he confirmed the amount, which is important. the commission believes that eur 11.5 million is sufficient to achieve what it has set out to do this year. if everyone is involved, including the media, this year can be a very big year for sport. i very much hope that the trend of declining importance of school sports will be reversed. this year we want to promote networking and cross-border cooperation. ladies and gentlemen, what we didn't want was for the little money to be used to fund an infinite number of research studies. there's always research, we don't need this year to do it. i think we should be satisfied with the research at the end, "what has this year brought?" but otherwise do not spend money on this. the council followed us here. my idea of organising a european competition in the run-up to the olympic games was also included - not in the treaty, but in a protocol. i am very happy about this and i very much hope that the commission will follow our request and launch a competition which will culminate in the winners of this competition being allowed to be present at the lighting of the olympic flame in olympia in 2004. that would be a highlight of the year of sports education. the commission has already made a number of proposals. we want to create a platform for educational activities in sports beyond borders, state educational institutions and organizations. we want to encourage crossborder initiatives and networks, and we need to create a pool of ideas through which exemplary projects and initiatives will be copied by as many people as possible during the preparation of 2003 and in 2004, in other words, best practices. the community project instrument is funded at 80%, and things done at national level alone are co-financed at 50%. i think this is a very appropriate way of highlighting the european dimension of this theme year. i would like to end by thanking the council and the commission and wishing all of us that we can bring the idea of this year of education through sport into our citizenship and that, at the end of the convention, it is wise to give sport a legal basis.

- the commission's statement on services of general interest in europe is on the agenda.
commission. - mr president, the question of public services is a subject of wide debate in europe and elsewhere, and the general trend over the last twenty years has been a change in the role of public authority, which no longer produces directly but regulates and sets the rules of the game. this is particularly the case in europe, where the objective - and necessity - of creating a single market has undoubtedly encouraged such a development. experience shows that the creation of a single market based on a system of healthy competition is fully compatible with social and economic concerns, of which services of general interest are one of the most concrete objectives. moreover, a higher level of competition in the economy as a whole has promoted the efficiency of services of general interest. the community's history has always been consistent. at each new stage in the construction of europe, there have been advances both towards greater freedom of movement of goods, persons, services and capital and towards greater solidarity and cohesion. each of the internal market's advances has gone hand in hand with the introduction of measures that ensure that the most vulnerable regions and citizens are not left behind. this was the case with the single act, and it was also the case in maastricht and amsterdam. the introduction of economic and social cohesion policy, consumer protection and environmental policy into the treaty, all of which are intended to accompany and balance opening-up and liberalisation strategies, is an example. article 16 of the treaty, introduced in amsterdam, explicitly recognises the role of services of general economic interest. it confirms the need to find a better way of ensuring a harmonious and coherent combination of the principles relating to services of general interest and the other treaty objectives, in particular the internal market and free competition. the commission has always recognised the essential role of services of general interest. in its 1996 communication on services of general interest in europe, it proposed a reference to the promotion of such services. the sectoral legislation adopted at community level for large network industries, particularly energy, has very ambitious objectives in terms of public services and quality. in addition, the commission has always applied competition and market rules in such a way that the provision and development of high-quality services of general interest are not impeded. as an example, i could mention the communication on public broadcasting, with its state aid rules, which was drawn up by mario monti and myself last year and which is an example of how the competition rules can be applied intelligently while giving governments a wide margin of manoeuvre to run the public service. services of general interest are also an essential component of the european social model. they contribute to the quality of life of citizens and are a prerequisite for the full enjoyment of many of their rights. in its report to the laeken council, the commission announced its intention, and i quote, 'to examine the suggestion to consolidate and specify in a framework directive the principles relating to services of general interest which underlie article 16 of the treaty'. the commission has decided to pursue this examination in the framework of a green paper. there are two main reasons for this approach. firstly, the issues raised are much broader and cannot be dealt with in a discussion which would be limited to a proposal for a framework directive. secondly, given the very different expectations and positions regarding the feasibility of a framework directive and the added value it would represent, it has become necessary to establish a baseline beforehand. nor should the technical and conceptual difficulties which the establishment of a framework directive will inevitably raise be underestimated. the green paper will enable the commission, firstly, to examine the appropriateness of drawing up a framework directive and, secondly, to launch a broad debate on the general question. the aim of this green paper is therefore not to delay the study of the feasibility of a framework directive. on the contrary, given the diversity of traditions, structures and positions in the member states, only a broad debate at european level can bring out enough common points to establish a general community framework. and, in parallel with the preparation of the green paper, we are continuing work on other issues, particularly in the area of the application of state aid rules and in the area of the evaluation of these services. this work could also make a useful contribution to the green paper. as regards the timetable, the green paper is expected to be adopted in march 2003 and the conclusions are expected to be drawn before the end of the year. that is the commission's statement on this matter. a clear violation of un minimum standards for the treatment of prisoners. in order to initiate the ordinary legal proceedings, the authorities demanded a deposit of the equivalent of eur 120 000. students of the tulku who tried to collect the money were arrested. this is a flagrant violation of international human rights. the authorities in china must comply with legal standards. the fight against terrorism, which is necessary and which we all support, cannot be fought without the rule of law. it is totally unacceptable to attribute the non-violent struggle for the exercise of tibetan religion and culture to an element of terrorism. on behalf of the epp-ed group, i call on the commission to bring these mistaken judgments immediately to the attention of the chinese in the human rights dialogue. enforcement based on unlawful conditions must be prevented and the granting of financial resources must be linked to progress in the human rights situation. i would ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to mobilize the embassies of your member states in beijing immediately to ensure that the accused are given a fair trial. the first measure must be to suspend the death penalty. and in conclusion, as president of the european parliament's intergroup on tibet, i would like to express my hope that the forces of reason will prevail in china and that our global commitment to the rule of law and human rights will be successful.
